= GitHub Workflows — what runs, and why some look duplicated

This directory holds the repo's CI/CD. A few workflows *look* like they overlap
but are deliberately distinct — documented here so the apparent duplication is
not "tidied away" into a real coverage gap.

== Hypatia: one live consumer, one suspended

* `static-analysis-gate.yml` -> `hypatia-scan` job — **live**. Runs Hypatia as
  part of the **gate**, then the `deposit-findings` job hands the results to the
  **gitbot-fleet learning** pipeline. This is the repo's working Hypatia
  coverage, on every PR and every push to `main`.
* `hypatia-scan.yml` — **suspended upstream, repurposed in the meantime.** This
  was the standalone scan, and it cannot call
  `standards/.github/workflows/hypatia-scan-reusable.yml`: that reusable uses
  `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@b96794f0…`, and standards' own
  `actions.lock` still records that leaf as `ref: <the pin's own SHA>`, which
  GitHub's lockfile validation rejects. Every job therefore died in "Set up
  job" — two seconds, no steps, no findings, on every event. standards#1271
  corrected nine such leaf entries and missed this one; measured on
  `metadatastician/selur` at a post-#1271 pin, still red. No pin avoids it.

Until that lands upstream, `hypatia-scan.yml` does the next most useful thing on
the same triggers: it squabbles the gate. `hyperpolymath/cicd-squabbler`
classifies each red check as self-win | escalate | assign-owner, and attributes
a `STARTUP_FAILURE` to the posture that actually caused it rather than to the
reusable's owner or to a security scan — precisely the mis-attribution this red
invited. It cannot cheat the gate: that repo's SPARK package proves
green ⇔ a required check actually ran and passed.

So Hypatia coverage was *not* traded away here; the second consumer was already
dead, and this restores a live job in its place. When the upstream leaf entry is
fixed, restore the standalone scan and re-point this file at the reusable.

== Secret scanning is single-sourced *in CI* — and two-tier overall

`secret-scanner.yml` calls the standards reusable (gitleaks + a Rust-secrets
check). An inline TruffleHog job was removed: the reusable deliberately retired
TruffleHog as redundant with gitleaks, so re-adding it was duplicated work, not
extra coverage.

**That retirement is scoped to CI.** The estate runs a deliberate *two-tier*
secret defence, and the second tier is not in this directory:

[cols="1,2,3"]
|===
| Tier | Engine | Where

| CI
| gitleaks (+ rust-secrets, shell-secrets)
| `secret-scanner.yml` -> standards reusable. Runs on pull_request and on push
  to main — i.e. on what has *already reached* the remote.

| Local
| TruffleHog
| `.github/hooks/scan-secrets.sh`, called by `.github/hooks/pre-push`. Runs *before* the
  push leaves the machine, on exactly the commits being pushed.
|===

Different engines at different checkpoints — the local tier is the only one that
can stop a key before it exists on a server, where revocation, not deletion, is
the only real remedy. Ratified by the owner, 2026-09-14: *"we [run] gitleaks on
github regularly but [run] trufflehog prior to pushes using the hooks system."*

*Do not delete `.github/hooks/scan-secrets.sh` as duplication of `secret-scanner.yml`.*
It is the other half of this design, not a second copy of this half. The two
tiers also cover for each other's blind spots: the hook excludes TruffleHog's
SonarCloud detector (it matches any 40-hex string, so every SHA-pinned action
reads as a secret — measured, 24 findings on a clean clone, all of them action
pins), and gitleaks in CI catches a genuine SonarCloud token as `generic-api-key`.

== SAST tools are complementary, not redundant

* CodeQL — **default setup**, enabled in repo settings, not a workflow here. An
  advanced `codeql.yml` used to sit alongside it, and the two are mutually
  exclusive: GitHub rejects an advanced configuration's SARIF while default
  setup is on, so the workflow ran the whole scan and threw the result away at
  upload — a permanent red that looked like a security failure. Lintel's carried
  no `queries:`, `config-file:` or `paths-ignore:`, so by
  hyperpolymath/standards#1031 AC5 nothing was lost by deleting it. Do not
  re-add `codeql.yml` without disabling default setup first.
* `sonarqube.yml` — SonarCloud (shell / JS surface; see `sonar-project.properties`).
* `static-analysis-gate.yml` — panic-attack + Hypatia gate (see above).

Each targets a different language/surface; together they cover what no single
analyser does.
